## Summary

The audit runner's READ path is cwd-independent (via prefix-to-sibling worklog scan in `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`), but its PERSIST path is not. `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` only injects `--worklog-dir` when an explicit value is passed; when the runner is launched from a non-project cwd (e.g. the skill install dir `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit`, which symlinks into this repo) WITHOUT `--worklog-dir`, every `wl` write in the persist path (`wl audit-set`, the priority-check `wl show`, `wl update --audit-text`) runs from the runner's cwd and resolves the WRONG worklog store (via git-root resolution of the symlinked path → SorraAgents), failing with `Work item not found: LP-...` even though the item exists.

Reproduced while auditing LP-0MS9GAN2P009KK6G (LLM Proxy project): reads (item fetch, children, ACs) all worked via the prefix scan, but all persistence failed with 'Work item not found' — and the Phase 1/2 models (launched with cwd=TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT=SorraAgents) could not read the target worklog, so parent AC evidence was assessed against the wrong repo scope (untracked `skill/start-proxy/` here) and every AC was wrongly marked unmet.

## Repro

```bash
cd ~/.pi/agent/skills/audit   # symlink into SorraAgents/skill
python3 ./scripts/audit_runner.py issue LP-<id>   # no --worklog-dir
# reads OK; persist fails: 'wl audit-set failed: Work item not found'
```

```bash
cd ~/.pi/agent/skills/audit && wl audit-set LP-0MS9GAN2P009KK6G --ready-to-close no --summary x --raw-output x --json
# => {success: false, error: Work

The audit skill (`skill/audit/`) has accumulated correctness gaps, performance issues, and code-quality debt from prior feature additions. This epic coordinates the systematic resolution of critical and high-priority defects followed by medium-priority refactors and polish.

- **Map (agent):** Executes `/skill:audit` on work items and expects fast, correct, reproducible audits.

## Summary

**Bug (stale-audit correctness gap).** `_compute_content_fingerprint` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, ~line 696) fingerprints only: git HEAD sha + work-item description hash + Key Files list. However, the audit's own file-scope manifest reads `git status --porcelain` (untracked/modified files) and the deep-analysis model reads the **working tree**, not just HEAD. So uncommitted code changes between audits do **not** invalidate freshness — the freshness gate can serve a stale audit for code that has since changed.

The docs claim "a change in ANY fingerprint component invalidates freshness", but working-tree state is not a component.

## Expected behaviour

Include the working-tree state in the fingerprint payload: a hash of `git status --porcelain` + `git diff --name-only HEAD` output (sorted, deterministic). A change in any uncommitted file, untracked file, or commit invalidates freshness; an untouched repo keeps the same fingerprint.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Modifying an uncommitted tracked file invalidates the fingerprint (stale audit → re-run).
2. Adding an untracked file invalidates the fingerprint.
3. Committing a change also invalidates (via the existing HEAD sha component).
4. An untouched working tree + unchanged description + unchanged Key Files keeps the same fingerprint (freshness preserved).
5. Unit tests cover all four cases; `python3 -m pytest skill/audit/tests/` passes green.
data.title: Include working-tree state in the audit content fingerprint (stale-audit gap)

**Summary:** The audit freshness gate (skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py `_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint`) keys freshness on the whole-repo git HEAD sha. ANY commit to the repo — even one touching files unrelated to the work item — changes HEAD, invalidates the content fingerprint, and forces a full two-phase re-audit. This caused a real false re-audit: NV-0MSP7P2PN009FT9U was audited "Ready to close: No" (AC5 partial), the content fingerprint was byte-identical on re-audit, yet an operator `/skill:audit` invocation re-ran the full pipeline (twice, dry-run and persisted), and the final persisted verdict flipped to "Ready to close: Yes" purely from model judgment variance on the same unverifiable AC — no new evidence. A freshness gate that actually asserted "the work is in HEAD" would have returned the stored verdict.

**Desired behavior:** freshness must be decided per work item, not per repo. If NO file touched by the work item has changed since the work was committed, the stored audit verdict stands — no re-audit, no model calls. If any touched file changed, the audit is stale and re-runs.

**User stories:**
- As an operator running `/skill:audit <id>` on an item whose work files are unchanged, I want the stored verdict returned in seconds so unrelated repo commits never trigger an expensive re-audit.
- As an operator, I want the gate to be strict about the work item itself: any change to files the item touched (or to its ACs/description/Key Files) must invalidate freshness.

**How to determine "files touched by the work item":**
1. Commits referencing the work item ID: `git log --all --grep=<id>` and/or the commit messages recorded on the work item comments (implement skill already records commit hashes). The union of files in those commits = touched files.
2. The Key Files section of the work item description (already parsed by `_extract_key_files`).
3. Fallback: if touched-file set cannot be determined (no commits recorded, git unavailable), fail open and re-run the pipeline (current behavior).

**Suggested approach (strict-mode fingerprint):** extend `_compute_content_fingerprint` to a payload of {touched-file set (paths + per-path current git blob hashes or latest commit touching each path), description_hash, key_files} instead of the bare repo HEAD sha. On freshness check, recompute per-path state; equality => fresh. Document trade-offs: the gate is no longer fail-open-cheap the same way, and tool-artifact rewrites (e.g. Unity batch runs rewriting ProjectSettings, see Nova AGENTS.md pitfall #4) must be tolerated — e.g. exclude known tool-artifact paths or accept that they invalidate freshness (safe direction: stale => re-run is never wrong, only wasteful).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] (AC1) Freshness gate decides freshness from the work item touched-file set, not the bare repo HEAD sha: a commit touching only unrelated files does NOT invalidate a stored audit with an unchanged fingerprint
- [ ] (AC2) Any change to a file in the touched-file set invalidates freshness and re-runs the pipeline
- [ ] (AC3) Work-item description/AC/Key Files changes still invalidate freshness (existing behavior preserved)
- [ ] (AC4) Touched-file set resolution falls back to fail-open (re-run pipeline) when it cannot be determined (no recorded commits, git unavailable)
- [ ] (AC5) Tool-artifact rewrites (e.g. ProjectSettings churn from Unity batch runs) are handled explicitly — either excluded from the touched-file comparison or documented as always-invalidating with a test
- [ ] (AC6) Unit tests cover: unrelated-commit freshness (AC1), touched-file change invalidation (AC2), description-change invalidation (AC3), and fail-open fallback (AC4)
- [ ] (AC7) Re-audit of NV-0MSP7P2PN009FT9U at unchanged state returns the stored verdict without re-running the pipeline (regression scenario from this issue)
data.title: Audit freshness gate: re-audit only when files touched by the work item changed

# Problem statement

When the implement skill encounters a work item that has already been implemented (e.g. the skill detects a commit where the work was completed but the item is in a wrong state/stage, or an audit identifies gaps in what was done), it should review the most recent audit report, fix any identified gaps inline, and proceed — rather than blindly re-implementing or silently skipping.

## Users

- **Agent executing `/skill:implement <id>`**: needs to handle the "already completed" case deterministically without manual intervention or blind re-implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Detect "already implemented"** — the implement skill recognizes when the work has already been completed (e.g. via commit history, status/stage mismatch, or an audit report indicating prior completion).
2. **Review audit report** — when already implemented is detected, fetch/review the most recent audit report for the item (`/skill:audit <work-item-id>`).
3. **Close gaps inline** — if the audit reveals gaps (unmet ACs, failing tests, missed requirements), fix them inline as part of the current item's implementation (option b per intake clarification, 2026-08-13) — NOT by creating new work items.
4. **Skip if clean** — if the audit shows no gaps, report the summary and skip further implementation (no re-work).
5. **Update documentation** — the implement skill's `SKILL.md` is updated to describe this new step and its logic.

## Constraints

- Changes are scoped to `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and corresponding doc hygiene tests.
- No new work items should be created for gaps — they are closed inline.
- Follow the existing implement skill structure (add a numbered step, consistent formatting).

## Existing state

The implement skill has no logic to detect when a work item has already been implemented. It proceeds through all steps regardless, which can lead to redundant work or missed gap remediation when an item's state/stage is out of sync with its actual implementation status.

## Desired change

Add a new step in the implement skill (between Step 3.1 "Definition gate" and Step 4 "Create a worktree") that:
1. Checks whether the item has already been implemented
2. If yes: reviews the latest audit report, identifies gaps, and fixes them inline
3. If no: proceeds to the normal workflow

## Risks & assumptions

- **Detection signal ambiguity** — "already implemented" must be driven by the implement skill's own output (it reports completion with a commit hash), not inferred from status alone; document the exact detection trigger in the skill.
- **Audit staleness** — the most recent audit report may predate later fixes; reuse a fresh audit (same guidance as existing Step 3: reuse a recent audit, else `/skill:audit <work-item-id>`).
- **Scope creep in inline gap-closing** — large gaps discovered via audit are potential new work items; keep inline fixes minimal and record extra opportunities as linked work items (discovered-from), not scope.
- **Dependency on audit output format** — logic reads the audit report; keep the reading step aligned with how the audit skill persists reports (`audit_report_<id>.md`).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Add the new step with detection logic and audit review procedure
- `tests/test_implement_skill_doc_hygiene.py` — Ensure doc hygiene tests still pass

## Related work

- SA-0MSAS108O009DYKT — audit skill must write audit report files with unique names
- SA-0MPGU5QG40040AWS — Move recent-audit bootstrap into implement skill
- SA-0MPMGES67002AP0Z — Implement per-child audit loop in Ralph

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What counts as 'already implemented'?" — Answer (operator): option d — the implement skill itself sometimes reports the work is already completed and points to a commit hash; in that situation the item is either (a) completed but in the wrong state/stage, or (b) a problem with the implementation was identified in an audit. Source: interactive reply, 2026-08-13.
- Q2: "What does 'close them' (the gaps) mean?" — Answer (operator): option b — fix the gaps inline as part of the current item's implementation, then proceed to in_review. No new work items for gaps. Source: interactive reply, 2026-08-13.
data.title: implement skill: if item already implemented, review latest audit report and close gaps (priority medium)

## Bug Report: implement skill report script path is broken

### Problem

The implement skill's final end-of-session report step references a report script at a path that does not exist in this repository.

### Expected Path

```
$(skill_path report)/scripts/render_report.py
```

This resolves to:
```
/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/report/render_report.py
```

### Actual Result

The file does not exist:
```
python3: can't open file '/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/report/render_report.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory
```

### Impact

- The implement skill's end-of-session report cannot be generated automatically
- Agents fall back to manual report rendering
- The `render_report.py` script may exist in the shared skills directory but is not found via `skill_path report`

### Required Fix

1. Verify the report skill location and script path
2. Update the implement skill's `SKILL.md` to reference the correct path
3. Or create the missing script at the expected location
4. Or update `skill_path report` to resolve to the correct directory

### References

- Implement skill: `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/SKILL.md` (Step: "Final step: standardized end-of-session report")
- Report skill reference: `../report/SKILL.md` within implement skill

---

## Root Cause (corrected during planning)

The original report's "Expected Path" is inaccurate. Verified during planning (2026-09-18):

- `$(skill_path report)` is resolved at runtime by the `skill_path` **shell shim** (`scripts/skill_path`), not by the pi `skill_path` tool. The shim mirrors the tool's search order and must be installed at `~/.pi/agent/bin/skill_path` (first on `PATH`).
- `render_report.py` **exists and runs** — it lives in the `report` skill's own directory, not in the implement skill:
  ```
  $ bash scripts/skill_path report
  /home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/report
  $ python3 "$(bash scripts/skill_path report)/scripts/render_report.py" --help   # exits 0
  ```
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to this repo's `skill/` tree.)
- **The defect:** the shim is **not installed** at `~/.pi/agent/bin/skill_path`. `~/.pi/agent/bin` is first on `PATH` but contains only `fd` and `rg`.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` symlinks `skill/`, `command/`, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` and installs config + the pre-push hook, but **never installs the shim** — so `~/.pi/agent/bin/skill_path` is missing on every machine that has run the installer.
- **Consequence:** `$(skill_path report)` expands to nothing in bash, so the documented command fails. The implement skill's `SKILL.md` invocation string (`$(skill_path report)/scripts/render_report.py`) is **already correct**; **no path edit to `skill/implement/SKILL.md` is required**.
- The shim was added in commit `ed2c25e8` (SA-0MT7U3NCB000T1SR) whose message/docs claim it is "installed at `~/.pi/agent/bin/skill_path`", but no install wiring shipped and the file is committed with mode `100644` (not executable).

## Required Fix (corrected)

1. `scripts/install_pi.sh`: install `scripts/skill_path` to `$HOME/.pi/agent/bin/skill_path` (`mkdir -p`, copy/install, `chmod +x`), idempotently; warn (fail-open, non-fatal) if `$HOME/.pi/agent/bin` is not on `PATH`.
2. Commit `scripts/skill_path` as executable (`100755`).
3. Install the shim on this machine and verify the implement skill's documented final-step command runs end-to-end from the project CWD.
4. Add a regression test so the missing-install defect cannot recur.
5. Update `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` to state that `install_pi.sh` installs the shim and that `~/.pi/agent/bin` must be on `PATH`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running the implement skill's documented final-step command verbatim from a project CWD renders the canonical report (exit 0, all report sections present) — no manual path resolution.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` installs `scripts/skill_path` to `$HOME/.pi/agent/bin/skill_path` as an executable, and a re-run is idempotent (shim intact, script exits 0).
- `skill_path <name>` resolves to the correct directory for every installed skill, and exits non-zero with a clear error message for an unknown skill.
- A regression test asserts the shim install wiring and resolution behaviour, so the defect cannot recur undetected.
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` states that `install_pi.sh` installs the shim and lists the `~/.pi/agent/bin` PATH prerequisite; the implement skill's documented invocation remains unchanged and is executed verbatim in the AC1 verification.

## Scope

**In scope:** install wiring for the `skill_path` shim in `scripts/install_pi.sh`; executable mode for `scripts/skill_path`; installing the shim on this machine; regression test; docs note.

**Out of scope:** changing the `$(skill_path <name>)/scripts/...` convention; editing `skill/implement/SKILL.md` or `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` (both already correct); moving `render_report.py`; changing the report template or the report-wiring hygiene tests.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Does the reported "Expected Path" (`~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/report/render_report.py`) match reality?
  Answer (planning, verified by investigation): No. `skill_path report` resolves to the `report` skill directory (`~/.pi/agent/skills/report`), where `render_report.py` already exists and runs. The implement skill's own `scripts/` directory has no `report/` subdir. Evidence: `bash scripts/skill_path report`, `python3 "$(bash scripts/skill_path report)/scripts/render_report.py" --help`.
- Q: Why did the command fail if the script exists?

## Summary

`audit_runner.py issue|batch --do-not-persist` currently skips **all** persistence, including the `auditedAt` timestamp. A successful dry-run validation (`Ready to close: Yes`) therefore leaves `auditedAt` stale. `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` (`auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`, `packages/shared/src/icons.ts:250`) stays `false`, so Herdr's selection list / DOWNTIME audit tier correctly re-queues the item as a stale-audit candidate and shows the ⏳ stale-passed state.

Observed on 2026-09-01 with `SA-0MSJ1BP9K009M8MV`: validated with `--do-not-persist --force` (`Ready to close: Yes`, deep analysis completed) but stored audit remained `2026-08-11T05:13:22Z` while `updatedAt` had advanced to `2026-09-01T18:33:14Z` (delta ~21 days via `herdr-downtime` claim + comments). Herdr was correct to show "out of date" — the dry-run never refreshed the freshness signal. Manual `wl audit-set` was required to make `updatedAt == auditedAt` and restore `isAuditFresh: true`.

## Problem

- `--do-not-persist` is documented as a dry run but gives no freshness guarantee; operators assume a passing validation will clear the stale flag, but it does not.
- Help text (`audit_runner.py:10656`, `10781` and `skill/audit/SKILL.md`) says only "Do not persist the audit report via wl update" — does not explain the Herdr staleness consequence nor the intended dry-run semantics.

## User story

As an operator running `audit_runner.py --do-not-persist` for a dry-run validation, I want a passing validation to still refresh the audit freshness timestamp so Herdr no longer shows the item as out of date, while the full raw report remains not persisted; the flag's help should make this contract explicit.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Freshness on dry-run success:** When `audit_runner.py issue <id> --do-not-persist` (and `batch --do-not-persist` for each drained item) completes with `Ready to close: Yes`, the work item's `auditedAt` is atomically updated to `now` (`updatedAt == auditedAt` in the same txn, `WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9` pattern) with `auditResult`/`readyToClose` reflecting the verdict, **without** persisting the full `rawOutput` markdown. `isAuditFresh` must be `true` immediately after, and `wl list --stage in_review --json` must show `auditedAt == updatedAt` and `isAuditFresh: true` (Herdr shows ✅ not ⏳ and excludes from audit tier). When the verdict is `Ready to close: No` / `partial` / failure, `auditedAt` is **not** bumped (fail-closed — a failed dry-run must not clear staleness).
2. **Help text updated:** `--do-not-persist` help on both `issue` and `batch` subparsers (and the `SKILL.md` flag table / persistence procedure) is updated to state: dry-run — full audit report is not stored, but on `Ready to close: Yes` the audit freshness timestamp (`auditedAt`/`auditResult`) is still persisted so Herdr/DOWNTIME treat the item as freshly audited; omit the flag to persist the full report. The previous terse "Do not persist the audit report via wl update" is replaced.
3. **No regression for full persist:** Without the flag, behavior is unchanged — full report + `auditedAt`/`auditResult` persisted atomically and lifecycle transitions (`completed`/`in_review` etc.) still apply. With the flag, lifecycle transitions still apply (flag does not suppress status/stage changes).
4. **Tests:** Unit/cli tests cover the new contract: (a) `--do-not-persist` + `Yes` bumps `auditedAt`/`auditResult` but leaves `rawOutput` empty/absent; (b) `--do-not-persist` + `No` does not bump; (c) help text contains the freshness/dry-run wording (mirrors `skill/audit/tests/test_skill_md_and_debug_logs.py` pattern for SKILL.md validation).
5. **Docs:** `skill/audit/SKILL.md` persistence section and runner flag docs updated to match the new flag semantics.

## Notes

- Discovered-from: `SA-0MSJ1BP9K009M8MV` (dry-run left Herdr stale, required manual `wl audit-set` to recover).
- Implementation hint: reuse the atomic `wl audit-set --ready-to-close yes|no` path (sets `updatedAt = auditedAt` in one txn) for the dry-run success case, passing summary but omitting `--raw-output`/`--audit-file` so `rawOutput` stays null. Do not call `wl update --audit-text` afterwards (that would bump `updatedAt` past `auditedAt + 60s` and re-stale).
- `batch` subcommand should apply the same rule per-item in the drain loop.
- Consider whether a new flag (e.g. `--truly-do-not-persist`) is needed for the rare case where even freshness must not be touched; default should be the freshness-preserving dry-run.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSJ1BP9K009M8MV` — effort-and-risk SKILL.md output path (the stale-audit observation)
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts:isAuditFresh` — `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:selectAuditCandidate` / `isAuditFresh` — audit tier selection
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:10656,10781` — flag definition
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py:495` — atomic `updatedAt = auditedAt` note

# Merge gate misses comment-referenced commits and treats foreign hex as candidates

## Summary

`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`: phases `_resolve_item_integration_evidence` and `_phase_fetch_and_cq` fail to use commit references stored only in comments, and treat arbitrary hex found in prose as cherry-pick candidates, producing a spurious merge-gate blocker and a false-negative audit.

Discovered during audit of OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S (open_source_llm, `--force` run, work already present in `origin/dev`).

## Symptom

- Work item has no feature branch and no commit in its description; its real implementation commit is referenced only in a comment (e.g. `235ef18` for OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S).
- Merge gate logs `integrating (branch=none, commits=[9b0f...])` then fails: `git cherry-pick 9b0f500f11f345ae106f727a8347f123bfa7fd9b -> rc=128 / fatal: bad object` and blocks the audit.
- `9b0f500f...` is a *foreign* autiobook reference pinned in the description (reference, not a commit in the owning repo). `235ef18` (the real commit) is never discovered.

## Root cause

1. **Comments not fetched early for merge gate.** `_phase_fetch_and_cq` loads the top-level `comments` from `wl show` into a separate binding, but `ctx.work_item.get("comments", [])` (or the equivalent) is still the default empty list when the merge gate resolves evidence, so commit shas referenced only in comments are never seen. Reproduction: `wl show OSL-... --children --json` has `workItem.comments` absent while top-level `comments` holds the Map commit.

2. **Over-broad hex extraction.** `re.finditer(r"\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b", desc, re.IGNORECASE)` picks up arbitrary hex strings (foreign repo refs, docs examples) and enqueues them as cherry-pick targets. The failing run treated `9b0f500f...` (from `9b0f500f11f...`, an autiobook pin) as a required candidate and failed closed when that object was absent.

3. **Interaction.** Because (1) left `commits=[foreign_hex]`, (2) caused the integration failure path; the item *was* already on `origin/dev` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor 235ef18 origin/dev -> yes`) but was rejected.

## Proposed fix

- Fetch and bind `comments` on `ctx` before `_phase_merge_gate` (or pass `comments` into `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`).
- Filter integration candidates to objects that actually exist or are already ancestors of `origin/dev` (e.g. `git cat-file -e <sha>` / `rev-parse --verify` check, or skip foreign shas that are not ancestors and not branch tips), so that documentation hex cited as reference does not force cherry-pick.
- Optionally, scope hex extraction to producer-attributed commit citations (e.g. `see commit <hex>`) rather than every hex token in prose.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A work item whose only commit citation is in a top-level comment (no branch, no 7+ hex in description) is correctly merged-gated: evidence resolves the commented commit and `containment` verifies it against `origin/dev`.
2. Hex tokens that are not objects in the owning repo (or are cited only as foreign-repo pinned references, not deliverable commits) do not cause `fatal: bad object` or a spurious merge-gate block.
3. Existing behaviour for feature-branch and description-referenced commits is preserved (regression tests).
4. No new behaviour breaks `wl show` clients: comment binding is done in the audit runner only.

## Evidence

- Failing run (`open_source_llm`, `235ef18` already in `origin/dev`):
  ```
  Merge gate: OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S work NOT present in origin/dev — integrating (branch=none, commits=["9b0f500f11f345ae106f727a8347f123bfa7fd9b"])
  git cherry-pick 9b0f500f11f345ae106f727a8347f123bfa7fd9b -> rc=128 / fatal: bad object
  ```
- Manual verification: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 235ef18 origin/dev -> yes`.
- Stored blocker audit: `wl audit-show OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S --json` (open_source_llm).

## Related

- Proposer work item: OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S (open_source_llm). See its audit trail and producer-review comment id OSL-C0MTQA3R4E0084LBY.
- Worktree remains at `open_source_llm/.worklog/worktrees/audit-merge-OSL-0MSS0KDLN0025R7S` (remove manually once triaged).

# Add TTS to the standup skill

**Headline:** Enhance the standup skill to automatically generate a WAV audio file of the full markdown standup report via the `speak` skill, saving both artifacts to a `standups/` directory.

## Problem Statement

The standup skill generates a markdown report but does not produce audio output. Users who want to listen to the standup report must read the markdown, limiting accessibility and convenience.

## Users

- **Standup participant** (agent): Wants to hear the standup report read aloud during a daily meeting without manually reading.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When `generate_standup.py` runs, it automatically generates a WAV file containing the full markdown standup report spoken aloud via the `speak` skill.
2. Both the markdown report and the WAV file are saved to a `standups/` directory at the project root (e.g., `<repo-root>/standups/`).
3. The markdown file is named with a date-based filename (e.g., `standup-2026-09-06.md`) and the WAV file shares the same base name (e.g., `standup-2026-09-06.wav`).
4. If the `speak` skill fails, the markdown file is still saved and the error is logged/warned — TTS failure does not prevent the report from being generated.
5. The `standups/` directory is created automatically if it does not exist.

## Constraints

- TTS invocation is automatic — no `--tts` flag needed.
- Full markdown report text is sent to the TTS engine.
- No automatic playback — only file generation.
- The `speak` skill script path should be resolved via `skill_path speak` (canonical resolution).
- Output directory: `standups/` at the project root (same resolution logic as `generate_standup.py` for the worklog directory).

## Existing State

- `generate_standup.py` already generates TTS-friendly text internally (`_format_item_tts`, `format_report`).
- The `speak` skill exists at `~/.pi/agent/skills/speak/` with both a bash script (`speak.sh`) and a Python timing wrapper (`speak.py`).
- The Python timing wrapper (`speak.py`) is preferred — it provides timing reports and keeps stdout clean.

## Desired Change

Modify `generate_standup.py` to:
1. After generating the markdown report, invoke the `speak` skill's Python wrapper with the full report text.
2. Save the markdown report to `standups/standup-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`.
3. The `speak` skill saves the WAV to `.pi/speak/` by default — capture or redirect its output so the WAV lands in `standups/standup-<YYYY-MM-DD>.wav` instead, or have `generate_standup.py` move/copy it.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` — Add TTS invocation and file-saving logic
- `$(skill_path speak)/scripts/speak.py` — Called to generate audio
- `standups/` — New directory for output files

## Risks & Assumptions

- **TTS API failure**: Network issues, rate limits, or service downtime may prevent WAV generation. Mitigation: markdown is always saved; TTS failure is non-fatal.
- **Long input text**: The full markdown report could be lengthy. Mitigation: `speak` skill has a 60-second timeout; if text exceeds the TTS API input limit, the call should fail gracefully with a warning.
- **Same-day runs**: If the standup is run multiple times on the same day, the date-based filename will collide. Mitigation: append a counter or timestamp (e.g., `standup-2026-09-06-2.md`, `standup-2026-09-06-2.wav`).
- **WAV file location**: The `speak` skill saves WAV to `.pi/speak/` by default. Mitigation: set `SPEAK_DIR` environment variable to `standups/` before invoking `speak.py`, or move/copy the file after generation.
- **Assumption**: The `speak` skill is available and functional at runtime. If not, the error is logged and the markdown report is still produced.

## Related Work

- None identified. This is a standalone feature.

## Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should TTS generation happen automatically every time, or with a flag?" — Answer (operator): "Every time." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Should the full markdown standup report or a condensed version be sent to TTS?" — Answer (operator): "Full markdown." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Should the WAV file be played automatically or just saved?" — Answer (operator): "Just saved." Source: interactive reply.

# implement.py finish hardcodes a 600s test timeout, so repos with a >10 min suite can never pass the pre-commit gate

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` runs its pre-commit verification through `run_cached(command, cwd=cwd, timeout=600, ...)` — a **hardcoded 600-second (10 min) per-command cap**, repeated at several call sites in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (npm path, repo-script path, pytest path, changed-scope path, final full-suite gate).

Repos whose full suite legitimately takes longer than 10 minutes can therefore **never** pass the gate. Tableau-Card-Engine (TCE) is the concrete case: its `npm --silent test` → `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` suite (unit + browser + tutorial E2E) takes **~17–19 minutes** (measured 1128s and 1024s on 2026-09-11).

Observed failure (TCE, work item CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC):

```
INFO: Running build...
INFO: Running test suite (changed scope)...
WARNING: Implement run_tests: npm tooling is not subsettable — running full scope ...
ERROR: Unhandled exception: Command '['npm', '--silent', 'test']' timed out after 600 seconds
INFO: Safety reset: CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC status in-progress -> open
```

Two distinct harms, the second arguably worse than the first:

1. **The gate always times out** for long-suite repos, so `finish` aborts and never commits/pushes/marks `in_review` — the work is done but cannot be landed through the standard workflow.
2. **The timeout masquerades as an implementation failure**: the safety reset silently flips the work item from `in_progress` back to `open` and un-claims it. The operator sees a bare "timed out after 600 seconds" with no hint that the suite is simply slower than the cap, and the item appears untouched/unclaimed.

Note the inconsistency: the *test skill* already solves this — `run_tests.py` reads `.pi/test-config.json`'s `timeoutPerCommand` via `suite_timeout_per_command()`, and TCE sets `{"timeoutPerCommand": 1500}` (25 min). Only `implement.py` ignores it.

## Users

- **AI agents** running `/skill:implement` in any repo whose full suite exceeds 10 minutes — they currently cannot complete the workflow without a manual out-of-band workaround.
- **Producers/reviewers** who are confused by a work item that silently reverts to `open` after a "failed" implementation run, and who cannot tell a real test failure from a timeout.
- **Repo maintainers** who already expressed the intended timeout in `.pi/test-config.json` and reasonably expect the implement gate to honour it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** `implement.py`'s pre-commit test gate reads the per-command timeout from the repo's `.pi/test-config.json` (`timeoutPerCommand`) when present and positive, and uses it for the verification command(s). When the key is absent, unreadable, or not a positive number, it falls back to the existing 600s default (behaviour for repos without the key is unchanged).
- **AC2:** The resolution is centralised — one helper (mirroring the test skill's `suite_timeout_per_command()`) feeds *every* test-gate call site (npm, repo-script, pytest, changed-scope, final full-suite gate, and the explicit `--timeout`-style overrides), so no call site silently keeps a divergent hardcoded cap.
- **AC3:** A repo whose full suite exceeds 600s (e.g. TCE, ~19 min) completes `implement.py finish` on the **first** attempt with **no** manual test-cache warm-up.
- **AC4:** On a genuine timeout, the failure is actionable and unambiguous: the message states the configured timeout, the command that timed out, and how to raise it (config key / flag). The safety reset to `open` is logged explicitly as "timed out — status reset to open, no test failure recorded", so a timeout is never mistaken for a test failure.
- **AC5:** Repos/configs without the new key are unaffected: the 600s default still applies, and a real test failure still blocks the commit and push.
- **AC6:** Unit tests cover: (a) `.pi/test-config.json` with a positive `timeoutPerCommand` → override used; (b) key absent → 600s default; (c) invalid values (0, negative, non-numeric, boolean, malformed JSON) → fallback with a warning; (d) a command that outlives 600s but fits under the configured cap is not killed.
- **AC7:** Documentation updated so the override is discoverable: the implement skill docs (`skill/implement/SKILL.md` and/or `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`) state that the pre-commit test gate honours `.pi/test-config.json` `timeoutPerCommand`, and the CLI `--help`/logging surfaces the effective timeout.
- **AC8:** Full SorraAgents test suite passes with the change (pytest + Node/bats, quiet mode).

## Constraints

- Target file: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (SorraAgents framework repo). The same helper module may be shared with the test skill's existing implementation — prefer reusing `suite_timeout_per_command()` over duplicating the parsing logic.
- Must not regress the recent scope-aware gating work (SA-0MT6BYQHB008DOGC): changed-scope runs, the final `--scope full` gate, and the pre-push full-suite hook all keep their current semantics; only the *timeout* is parameterised.
- The test cache contract must be preserved: a timeout must not poison the cache (no exit-0/exit-124 entry stored as a legitimate pass).
- Do not change the safety-reset-to-`open` invariant itself (it is correct) — only its messaging/attribution when the cause is a timeout.

## Evidence

- Reproduced in TCE work item **CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC** (upgrade hand-first click flow), 2026-09-11: first `implement.py finish` attempt aborted with the 600s timeout and reset the item to `open`; a second attempt succeeded in ~105s once the full-scope test cache had been pre-populated.
- TCE's `.pi/test-config.json` is `{"timeoutPerCommand": 1500}` — the value the gate should have used.
- Measured TCE full-suite durations: 1128s (pre-commit) and 1024s (post-push), both PASS.

## Workaround currently required (until fixed)

Pre-populate the full-scope test cache using the test skill (which honours `timeoutPerCommand`), after which `implement.py finish` hits the cache and skips execution:

```bash
python3 ~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py --scope full --timeout 1500 --project-root "$PWD"
```

This adds ~19 minutes of mandatory manual step to every implement run in TCE and relies on undocumented knowledge.

## Related work items

- **SA-0MSI8YLTN0007KN8** (completed) — "implement.py finish hardcodes npm run build, blocking non-node repos": same class of defect (hardcoded tooling assumption in `finish`), useful precedent for the fix shape and test approach.
- **CG-0MTXKIIRV009MJWG** (TCE) — mirror item filed in the TCE worklog; close as duplicate/relocate once this item is resolved.
- **SA-0MT6BYQHB008DOGC** — scope-aware test gating (changed scope + final full gate + pre-push full suite), whose call sites this change parameterises.

## Non-goals

- Reducing the runtime of any repo's test suite (TCE suite runtime is a separate concern).
- Changing the test cache TTL, the scope semantics, or the pre-push hook behaviour.

# Ship skill: parent-coverage and out-of-scope rules for child audits in the final-validation gate

## Summary

The ship skill's **final-validation gate (Step 6)** sweeps **ALL** `in_review` items — top-level *and* children — and blocks on any child whose audit is missing/stale/failing. This contradicts Steps 2 (audit readiness) and 5 (producer review), which are deliberately **top-level scoped**, and the documentation's own statement that *"Child items are covered by their parent's audit and never block."*

The result is that a release can be blocked by child audit gaps that are either (a) already covered by a passing parent audit, or (b) outside the release scope because the parent is not `in_review` at all.

## Discovery (source)

Surfaced during the Tableau-Card-Engine (TCE) dev→main release on 2026-09-15. The gate reported 60 non-passing `in_review` items; **all 60 were children** under 14 parents:

- **11 parents** were top-level `in_review`/`completed` with **passing audits** (`readyToClose === true`) — covering **52** of the children.
- **3 parents** were at `plan_complete`/`open` (not `in_review`) — covering **8** of the children; these work-streams are not part of the release.

The operator's ruling (to be encoded): parent-covered children are **satisfied**; children of non-`in_review` parents are **excluded** from the release scope.

## Goal

As a release manager using the ship skill, I want the final-validation gate to treat a child's audit as satisfied when its parent has a **fresh passing** audit, and to **exclude** children whose parent is not `in_review`, so a release is never blocked by child audit gaps that are already covered by the parent's audit or outside the release scope — while still catching genuine, uncovered child audit failures.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Parent coverage:** the final-validation gate treats a child as `passing` (non-blocking) when its parent (resolved via `parentId`) has a **fresh passing** audit (`readyToClose === true`), and records the coverage in the gate report (e.g. "N child(ren) covered by passing parent audit <parentId>").
2. **Out-of-scope exclusion:** the final-validation gate **excludes** a child whose parent is not in stage `in_review` (i.e. the parent is not part of the release) — such children never block, and are reported as excluded with the parent id and stage.
3. **Conservative fallback:** parent coverage does **not** apply when the parent audit is missing, stale, transient, or failing. An uncovered child with a missing/stale/failing audit still blocks exactly as today (exit 12).
4. **Top-level behaviour unchanged:** top-level `in_review` items are evaluated exactly as today; the new rules apply only to children.
5. **Recursion/ancestors:** coverage resolves through the parent chain safely — a child of a child (grandchild) is covered by its nearest `in_review` ancestor with a passing audit; a non-`in_review` ancestor excludes the subtree.
6. **Hermetic unit tests** (injectable boundaries; no live `wl`/`audit_runner`): (a) covered child passes; (b) uncovered child with a failing audit still blocks; (c) child of a non-`in_review` parent is excluded; (d) parent with a stale audit does not cover; (e) grandchild resolves via nearest passing ancestor.
7. **Documentation:** `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` describe the parent-coverage and out-of-scope rules and their precedence, so the decision is repeatable without operator intervention.
8. **Exit codes unchanged:** the gate still exits 12 on genuine uncovered failures; successful runs still exit 0.

## Precedence

For each child, evaluate in order:
1. Parent not in `in_review` → **excluded** (not part of the release).
2. Parent (nearest `in_review` ancestor) has a fresh passing audit → **covered/satisfied**.
3. Otherwise → evaluate the child's own audit (missing/stale/transient → auto-remediate; failing → block).

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js`: resolve each child's `parentId` chain, fetch the parent's stage and audit (`wl show <parentId> --json` / `wl audit-show`), and apply the precedence above.
- Reuse the existing `classifyAudit`/`isAuditStale` helpers for the parent audit; add a bounded parent cache to avoid repeated `wl` calls.
- Add `coveredItems` and `excludedItems` to the returned report; keep `blockingItems` semantics unchanged.
- Unit tests in the ship skill's test suite using the existing injectable command boundaries.

## Deliverables

- Updated `check-final-validation.js` with parent-coverage + out-of-scope logic
- Hermetic unit tests for all AC6 cases
- `SKILL.md` + `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` documentation updates

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js`
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` (reuse `classifyAudit` / `isAuditStale`)
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md`
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`

## Notes / Assumptions

- "Approved for release" for a parent means: top-level (or ancestor) in stage `in_review` with a fresh passing audit.
- This changes gate *scoping*, not audit *rigour*: a genuinely uncovered child audit gap still blocks.
- Discovered during TCE release; the operator applied the rule manually (parent-coverage audit records) for that release pending this change.


## Additional finding — recursive force-close defeats the exclusion rule (2026-09-15)

During the same TCE release, the close-work-items step (`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` → `wl close <id> --force --reason "Shipped in v<version>"`) force-closed **candidates recursively**, sweeping descendants that were NOT release candidates — including an explicitly **excluded** subtree:

- Excluded child `CG-0MU1SJ6D2008WAW2` (parent `CG-0MTT7FC7A000AA58`, not `in_review`) was closed because its *grandparent* `CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128` was a shipped top-level candidate; the recursive `--force` close ignored both the exclusion and the intervening non-`in_review` parent.
- Its excluded parent `CG-0MTT7FC7A000AA58` was swept to `done` in the same operation.

Both were manually restored (`open`/`plan_complete` and `in-progress`/`plan_complete`); the release itself was unaffected. This means the exclusion rule (AC2) is only honoured if the close step is also scoped.

### Additional acceptance criteria

9. **Scoped close:** the close-work-items step closes only items in the release candidate set (and, when recursing, only descendants that are themselves candidates or are explicitly included) — a `--force` recursive close must not close descendants outside the candidate set. An excluded subtree nested beneath a shipped item survives the release intact.
10. **Collateral detection/report:** the close step reports any descendant it would close outside the candidate set, and any such closure is either refused or recorded as an explicit, reversible exclusion decision.

### Additional test cases (extends AC6)

- A candidate whose subtree contains a non-candidate descendant (e.g. `plan_complete`) closes the candidate but leaves the descendant untouched.
- An excluded subtree nested under a shipped candidate survives a full release.

# RCA: audit Phase 1 / Phase 2 reliability

**Discovered-from:** SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 (audit, 2026-09-15).

## Goal

Determine why the audit pipeline (Phase 1 screening and Phase 2 deep analysis)
frequently fails or degrades, identify the common failure modes from the debug
corpus and stored audit reports, and produce a prioritised set of reliability
recommendations with follow-up work items for accepted fixes.

## Problem

Audits routinely end `Ready to close: No` for *infrastructure* reasons rather
than genuine code defects, forcing manual re-audits and blocking releases. In
SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 the runner reported `No` even though all code ACs were
satisfied, because of concurrency saturation (Phase 1 parent screening never
ran), in-main-slot child screens left pending, and a 600s full-suite timeout.
There is no single RCA that quantifies these modes or ranks fixes.

## Method and evidence sources

1. Debug corpus: `~/.audit_debug/<project>/audit_debug_*.jsonl` (raw Pi
   streams + the logged `reason`).
2. Stored audit reports: `worklog/data:.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl`
   (`rawOutput` per item; counts below are from a 2026-09-15 export).
3. Runner source: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
   (`_call_pi`, `_call_pi_and_maybe_log`, `_extract_json_array`,
   Phase 1/Phase 2 call sites) and `skill/scripts/pi_utils.py`
   (`extract_pi_text`).

## Preliminary findings (to be verified and extended by this item)

### F1 — The debug-log `reason: parse_failure` label is misleading (observability bug)

`_call_pi_and_maybe_log` sets `reason = "parse_failure"` whenever the Pi
result carries `raw_stdout`/`raw_stderr` — but `raw_stdout` is present on
**every successful call**. Corpus: 19,663 debug files / 39,619 `parse_failure`
entries vs only 26 `provider_error`. Re-running `extract_pi_text()` +
`_extract_json_array()` over real-project logs (285 files) shows ~92-95% of
`parse_failure` entries **parse cleanly** (`parent` 158/172, `phase2_deep`
93/98, `false-positive-screen` 41/43). Any failure analysis keyed on this
label is invalid.

### F2 — Genuine JSON-contract failures are real but rarer (~5-8%)

34 genuine failures in real-project logs. Dominant shape: the model stops
(`stopReason: stop`) after narrative analysis and never emits the required
JSON array; 16/34 produced <200 output tokens (empty or truncated text).
Handler: the call sites fall back to a conservative `partial` verdict.

### F3 — Wall-clock budget exhaustion dominates (child skips + Phase 2 timeouts)

Stored reports: `Manual audit required` ~350 (dominated by `Skipped due to
audit timeout` ~176 and `Audit runner skipped this child after Ns ... to avoid
the parent process timeout` ~100+); `Pi model call timed out after 1800s`
16; `pending deep code review` 88. Parent-process timeout budgets observed
vary widely across runs (~120s, 900s, 1500s, 3110s) — inconsistent right-sizing.

### F4 — Concurrency saturation aborts Phase 1

`Audit concurrency limit reached ... queue saturated` ~12. In
SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 the Phase 1 parent screen waited 90s, got no host-wide slot
(concurrent audits), and returned `unmet` — no Pi call was made at all.

### F5 — In-main-slot child screens leave children unverified

Default `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT=true` emits `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]`
prompts for the main session. If the session does not run them, child ACs stay
`partial (pending main-session review)` and the parent cannot close — the
2026-09-15 SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 run did exactly this.

### F6 — Provider errors

`Pi provider error` 15 (generic "provider error" 75). Retried with backoff
(`_PI_MAX_RETRIES`); Phase 2 passes `max_retries=1`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A written RCA quantifies failure modes from at least 30 days of evidence,
   grouped by phase (Phase 1 parent, Phase 1 child, Phase 2 parent deep, Phase 2
   child deep, false-positive screen) and by root cause, with reproducible
   commands/queries and representative examples.
2. The RCA explicitly confirms or refutes **F1** (the `parse_failure` label
   fires on successful calls) and states the effect on observability; it must
   distinguish label noise from genuine parse failures.
3. Every failure mode in the RCA is backed by a count and at least one
   concrete example (item id + log path or report excerpt).
4. A prioritised recommendation list is produced (impact x effort), each item
   naming the concrete change, the expected reliability effect, and the
   observable signal that would confirm improvement.
5. Recommendations cover, at minimum: JSON-output contract robustness
   (e.g. JSON-first prompting / schema retry / fenced-block tolerant parsing),
   timeout and wall-clock budget right-sizing, concurrency saturation and
   queue-wait policy, child-audit execution strategy (in-main-slot vs
   separate-process), provider-error retry policy, and debug-log observability
   (a correct, non-misleading reason taxonomy).
6. Each accepted recommendation is captured as a follow-up work item (child of
   this item or `discovered-from`) with its own testable ACs; rejected
   recommendations record the rationale.
7. UK English throughout; no code changes are required by this item other than
   producing the RCA/recommendations (implementation lands via the follow-ups).

## Constraints

- Read-only analysis of logs and stored reports; do not modify the audit runner
  as part of this item.
- Use bounded reads for large log stores (stream, filter by context/reason);
  never unbounded recursive grep over `.worklog/`.
- Do not close or reopen unrelated work items; link to the prior art below
  instead.

## Related work (prior art — evaluate, do not duplicate)

- **SA-0MPOGKY8U007K206** — add debug logging for Pi responses (introduced the
  current reason label).
- **SA-0MQ4GGKUR00752Z8** — parse JSON array from mixed analysis+JSON response.
- **SA-0MRW8T054007QH0A** — audit runner bugs: child filtering, JSON parse
  fallback, silent failure.
- **SA-0MSL1Z15600760KC** — consolidate duplicate Pi JSON-stream parsers (open).
- **SA-0MSF4AFXF000M5DN** — right-size the parent-timeout guard for multi-child
  parents.
- **SA-0MSABZO2T004B95X** — make the cumulative elapsed-time guard configurable.
- **SA-0MSGEAZMC009LHKL** — fail immediately on audit concurrency limit.
- **SA-0MS0SQQTW006GNX9**, **SA-0MS3FNIUA00385DE**, **SA-0MQPQX57I0055ITT** —
  Phase 2 deep-analysis timeout.
- **SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE** — in-main-slot child audit mode.
- **SA-0MU2PXILZ000RPR1** — raise full-suite per-command timeout (this session).
- **SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0** — audit that motivated this RCA.

**Parent:** SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL (RCA: audit Phase 1/Phase 2 reliability)
**Discovered-from:** SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 (audit, 2026-09-15).

## Problem

`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_call_pi_and_maybe_log` sets
`reason = "parse_failure"` whenever the Pi result carries `raw_stdout`/`raw_stderr`.
But `raw_stdout` is present on **every successful call**, so the debug log
labels successful calls as parse failures.

Evidence (2026-09-15 corpus scan):

- 19,663 `~/.audit_debug/**/audit_debug_*.jsonl` files; 39,619 entries with
  `reason: parse_failure` vs only 26 with `provider_error`.
- Re-running `extract_pi_text()` + `_extract_json_array()` over real-project
  logs (285 files) shows ~92-95% of `parse_failure` entries parse cleanly:
  `parent` 158/172, `phase2_deep` 93/98, `false-positive-screen` 41/43.
- Genuine parse failures in real-project logs: ~34.

Consequence: any failure analysis keyed on this label is invalid, and the
false funnel made the reliability RCA (SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL) far harder.

## Desired change

Replace the blanket label with an accurate taxonomy: a neutral default reason
(e.g. `call_trace`) for calls that returned, plus an explicit parse-outcome
flag set by the call site, and `parse_failure` only when the expected JSON
shape genuinely could not be extracted.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_call_pi_and_maybe_log` no longer records `reason: parse_failure` for a
   call whose output was successfully parsed at the call site.
2. The debug entry carries an explicit parse-outcome field (e.g. `parse_ok:
   true|false`) and a neutral reason for successful calls.
3. A genuine parse failure is still recorded distinctly (labelled
   `parse_failure` or equivalent) and is machine-distinguishable from a
   successful call.
4. Provider errors remain labelled `provider_error` and are not conflated with
   parse failures.
5. Unit tests cover: successful call -> not `parse_failure`; genuine parse
   failure -> labelled; provider error -> `provider_error`.
6. `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` documents the reason taxonomy; existing
   debug-log tests/consumers are updated.

# R2 — Harden the audit JSON contract (JSON-first prompt + tolerant extraction + bounded re-ask)

**Parent:** SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL (RCA: audit Phase 1/Phase 2 reliability)
**Discovered-from:** SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 (audit, 2026-09-15).

## Problem

Genuine JSON-contract failures are rarer than the debug label suggests
(~5-8%), but they are real and avoidable. In real-project logs, 34 genuine
failures; the dominant shape is the model stopping (`stopReason: stop`) after
narrative analysis and never emitting the required JSON array, with 16/34
producing <200 output tokens (empty or truncated text). Pi also routinely
wraps the array in Markdown code fences (```` ```json ... ``` ````) with prose
around it.

Prior art: SA-0MQ4GGKUR00752Z8 (parse mixed analysis+JSON),
SA-0MRW8T054007QH0A (JSON parse fallback), SA-0MSL1Z15600760KC (consolidate Pi
JSON parsers, open).

## Desired change

Make the JSON contract JSON-first and tolerant, and add a single bounded
"return only the JSON array" re-ask before the conservative `partial`
fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Phase 1 parent/child and Phase 2 parent/child prompts request the JSON
   array first (or only), with prose after, and restate the exact schema and
   the required keys.
2. `_extract_json_array` tolerates leading/trailing prose and Markdown code
   fences and selects the intended balanced array; covered by unit tests using
   real fenced/prose fixtures captured from the debug corpus.
3. On extraction failure, exactly one bounded re-ask ("return only the JSON
   array") is issued before falling back to `partial`; the re-ask is
   observable (context `verdict_reask`) and bounded by the per-call budget.
4. A genuine parse-failure rate is measured over a re-run corpus (>=20 items)
   and recorded on this item; it is reduced relative to the pre-change
   baseline.
5. Verdict semantics are unchanged: a persistent failure still falls back to
   the conservative `partial`, never `met`/`Yes`.
6. Full project test suite passes.

- UK English.

# R5 — Enforce the child-audit execution contract (no silent pending child screens)

**Parent:** SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL (RCA: audit Phase 1/Phase 2 reliability)
**Discovered-from:** SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 (audit, 2026-09-15).

## Problem

With the default `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT=true`
(SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE), the runner emits `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` prompts
for the main session instead of executing child screens. If the session does
not run them, child ACs remain `partial (pending main-session review)` and the
parent cannot close — with no explicit gate or resume. The 2026-09-15 audit of
SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 ended in exactly this state.

## Desired change

Define and enforce the child-audit execution contract so a parent audit either
completes all child verdicts or surfaces an explicit, actionable, resumable
gate — never a silent `partial`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The contract is documented in `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and
   `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`: either the runner executes child
   screens itself, or in-main-slot mode must surface an explicit
   "N child screens pending" gate that prevents a `Yes` verdict and closure.
2. A parent audit never ends with child ACs `partial (pending main-session
   review)` presented as a normal result: the pending state is explicit,
   actionable (names the child ids and how to complete them), and blocks
   `Ready to close: Yes`.
3. A persisted/resumable signal records which child screens remain, so a
   subsequent run completes them without a full re-audit.
4. Tests cover both modes: separate-process executes the child screens;
   in-main-slot emits the gate and the parent cannot report `Yes` with pending
   children.
5. Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- UK English.
- Do not silently change the default mode; make whichever default is chosen
  safe (explicit gate or in-process execution).

# Intake Brief: Critical repo wipe by destructive 'init' commit — test-isolation failure

## Problem Statement

The test fixture `TestRootFileOnlyRepoManifest._init_repo` in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py` executed against the live repository root instead of its designated `tmp_path`, producing commit `2c30dbfe` ("init") that deleted 472 files / 138,007 lines. The local `dev` branch was corrupted by a fast-forward pull of this commit. The live checkout has been recovered, the fixture has been guarded, and the destructive commit is now unreachable from all local refs.

## Users & User Stories

- **Agent/operator:** "When tests run in a loaded multi-agent environment, test fixtures must never be able to commit into the live repository — I need the test suite to fail safely, not silently destroy code."
- **Team:** "After a test-isolation incident, the repo must be recoverable with minimal manual intervention, and a guard must exist to prevent recurrence."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Local `dev` branch restored to full repository tree** — verified by `git rev-parse HEAD` pointing at a valid commit on `origin/dev` and `git status` clean.
2. **Destructive commit `2c30dbfe` unreachable from any local branch** — verified by `git for-each-ref --contains 2c30dbfe` returning empty.
3. **Test-isolation guard added to `TestRootFileOnlyRepoManifest._init_repo`** — the fixture now asserts `tmp_path` is not inside a git repository before executing `git init`; a regression test `test_init_repo_refuses_live_repo_tmp_path` verifies this guard.
4. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.
5. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- The guard must not break legitimate uses of `_init_repo` with isolated tmp dirs.
- Recovery steps must not disturb other agents' worktrees or local branches (other than the corrupted `dev` on the main checkout).
- The destructive commit must be completely pruned from local refs.

## Existing State

- `origin/dev` was clean at `74bd0437` when the incident was detected; the damage was local-only.
- The fixture's placeholder filenames (`install.sh`, `remote`, `sshl`, `update`, `ai.home.conf`, `tests/test_a.py`) and git identity (`T <t@t.com>`, commit message "init") exactly matched commit `2c30dbfe`.
- Recovery was executed by resetting `dev` to `origin/dev` (reflog confirms `74bd0437 dev@{7}: branch: Reset to origin/dev`).
- The fixture isolation guard (SA-0MU8EKJYY007PT42) was implemented and verified.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py` — Guard at lines 495-535: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` check with `AssertionError` on live repo root; regression test at line 606.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py` — Class docstring updated with incident context.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MU8EKJYY007PT42**: "Dangerous test fixture: TestRootFileOnlyRepoManifest._init_repo can commit against the live repo" — completed/in_review, all 3 ACs met, guard + regression test delivered (commit `127e2ec5`).
- **SA-0MU8CD4V3002WL7N**: "skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py failing tests" — completed/in_review (pre-existing failures now closed).
- **SA-0MU0X9CRI009QKKK**: "Quality Improvement - Refactoring" — open/plan_complete; the stale worktree branch that held 2c30dbfe has been re-pointed.
- **SA-0MU7KKJSW006AD5D**: "[test-failure] TestBudgetExhaustionRecording" — parent item, blocked (pre-existing condition, unrelated to recovery).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope**: This item covers incident recovery and the test-isolation guard. The fixture change is delivered via SA-0MU8EKJYY007PT42.
- **Assumption**: All related documentation (class docstring, code comments) was updated as part of SA-0MU8EKJYY007PT42.
- **Risk**: A similar test-isolation vulnerability may exist in other fixtures. This is a separate investigation opportunity.
- **Scope creep**: Additional fixtures should be audited separately; this item covers `_init_repo` only.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Authorise local main-checkout reset to `origin/dev`?" — A: Recovery already executed by another agent; reflog confirms `git checkout -B dev origin/dev` at 74bd0437. Source: local git reflog.
- Q: "Should the fixture change be handled here or via a separate work item?" — A: Handled via separate item SA-0MU8EKJYY007PT42, now completed/in_review. Guard + regression test verified.
- Q: "Was the destructive commit ever pushed to a shared remote branch other than dev/main?" — A: Verified via `git for-each-ref --contains 2c30dbfe` — no refs contain the commit. `origin/dev` and `origin/main` are clean.

# Audit runner: pre-review child with `inherited_pass` bypasses children-stage block and summary claims "all children in in_review/done"

Discovered during the audit of `CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I` (Tableau-Card-Engine) — `discovered-from:CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I`.

## Problem Statement
The audit runner can report **"Ready to close: Yes"** for a parent work item that has a **critical, pre-review-stage child** (e.g. an auto-triaged `test-failure` item at `intake_complete`), and the report summary falsely claims *"All children are in in_review or done stage."* This produces a false-positive closure verdict.

## Evidence (reproduction)
- Audited item: `CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I` (Tableau-Card-Engine), audit run 2026-09-20.
- The runner auto-executed the full suite (F3 cache-miss path). The unit vitest stage was **SIGKILLed (exit 137)**.
- The test skill triaged this into `CG-0MUA2UWY7002KUQR` — a **critical `test-failure` bug** created as a **child** of the audited item at `status: open`, `stage: intake_complete`.
- The runner then reported `Ready to close: Yes` with summary: *"All children are in in_review or done stage."*
- The persisted report's `## Children Status` **does** render the child as `CG-0MUA2UWY7002KUQR — open/intake_complete` with verdict `met` ("Inherited from parent pass") — directly contradicting the summary.

## Root Cause
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (~9855-9861, `if not parent_gaps:` branch): when the parent passes with no gaps, **every** child gets `cr["inherited_pass"] = True` and `cr["child_audit_ready"] = True` — with **no stage guard**. The only guard is `_child_content_changed`, which is false for a brand-new child.
- `audit_runner.py:4207`: `all_children_reviewed = all(c.get("stage") in ("in_review","done") or c.get("inherited_pass") ...)` — `inherited_pass` exempts a **pre-review** child from the blocking children-stage check.
- `audit_runner.py:4333`: the summary unconditionally appends *"All children are in in_review or done stage."* when `all_children_reviewed` is true, even when a child is actually at `intake_complete`/`idea`/`plan_complete`.

## Expected Behaviour
- A child in a pre-review stage (`idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`) MUST block parent closure, per the documented rule ("only pre-review stages block") and `SA-0MRL8W6V7006LH5I`.
- `inherited_pass` (parent-first pass-through, `SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F`) must not exempt a pre-review child from the stage check — at minimum it must not apply to a child created during the audit run (auto-triaged `test-failure`).
- The summary text must be accurate: if any child is not in `in_review`/`done`, say so and produce "Ready to close: No".

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A parent with any non-deleted child in `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete` reports "Ready to close: No" and names the blocking child, regardless of `inherited_pass`.
- [ ] `inherited_pass` is only applied to children in `in_review`/`done` (or explicitly exempted with a documented rationale), never to pre-review children.
- [ ] The summary's "All children are in in_review or done stage." line is only emitted when that is actually true; otherwise it names the blocking children.
- [ ] Regression test: auditing a parent whose child sits at `intake_complete` (with `inherited_pass` otherwise set) yields "Ready to close: No".

## Secondary observation (may warrant a follow-up item)
- AC5 ("Full project test suite must pass") was marked `met` by the Phase 1 model even though the runner's own suite execution was killed (exit 137). The documented fail-open semantics say execution-dependent ACs should stay `partial` on a red/error run. Confirm whether a red/killed run must force `partial` on execution-dependent ACs.

## Related Work
- `SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E` — Audit runner circular dependency (child verdict blocks parent regardless of stage) — completed; the inverse problem.
- `SA-0MRL8W6V7006LH5I` — If a child audit is not ready to close then the parent must also be marked not ready to close — completed.
- `SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F` — parent-first pass-through (`inherited_pass`).

## Key Files
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — ~4201-4214 (children-stage check), ~4333 (summary text), ~9855-9861 (`inherited_pass` assignment).
